newsitem.title: UK: LME copper backwardation shoots out amid tightness.
newsitem.headline: LME copper backwardation shoots out amid tightness.

text.p: Copper maintained a firmer tone on Monday afternoon after aggressive third Wednesday pricing earlier in the day pushed out the nearby backwardation by $100.
Zinc also took a constructive step by leaping over the psychological $1,500 resistance level into new 6-3/4 year highs, while other metals ended the afternoon kerb mixed.
The centre of attention was copper, which entered the first prompt date of a two-week span of tightness with a bang as expected, traders said.
Cash/threes backwardation widened dramatically to $240/$260 by the end of the kerb compared to Friday's $130/$140.
Three months copper was also firmer and near the day's highs at $2,315, up $13, after easily hurdling $2,300 resistance earlier in the day.
LME chief executive David King said at the midday session that he continues to watch the copper market, noting that trading during the rings was "totally orderly".
The next two weeks are expected to remain tight and traders suspect the long in the market is an investment interest, while the shorts include a big Asian player.
Analysts said the question is whether tightness will start building up in August.
"There was a lot of pricing and a lot of shortcovering and the key is whether it can hold up here now," said William Adams of Rudolf Wolff.
But he added that the backwardation was hefty and could encourage any spare metal to emerge from the woodwork.
Stocks rose by 2,075 tonnes on Monday.
Zinc's drama was slower in coming, but prices finally pushed above $1,500 in inter-office trading just before the afternoon kerb. The cash/threes spread was near level at the end of the kerb.
A patch of tightness in September is seen underpinning the three months price, which ended the kerb $16 firmer at $1,502.
But traders said producer selling would probably cap the market around the $1,500 level, at least temporarily.
Aluminium went quiet in the afternoon after the pricing was finished, and traders said it ran into resistance at the previous support level between $1,590-$1600.
It finished the kerb at $1,584, up just $2 from Friday and off from the high of $1,597.
Lead had a weak finish at a $9 lower $658. It initially surged to a high of $674.50 but was unable to maintain momentum when pricing selling emerged in the afternoon.
Nickel also finished lower at $6,880, down $85, failing to recover from a burst of cash selling in the midday session.
Tin was $40 firmer at $5,590, but alloy was quiet and softer at $1,435/440, compared to $1,450.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
